sex + birthDate resolve to a life-stage key, which is what selects the RDA/AI/UL column out of nutrients.json. Changing them on the settings screen visibly re-personalises every target.

goalModes.name: General health
goalModes.description: Balanced targets with an emphasis on plant diversity. The default.
goalModes.evidenceNote: Dietary-pattern evidence (Mediterranean and DASH trials) is among the strongest in nutrition. The plant-diversity target of 30 species per week comes from the American Gut Project, which is observational — it is a reasonable heuristic, not a proven threshold.

goalModes.name: High protein
goalModes.description: Targets 1.6–2.2 g protein per kg bodyweight and surfaces per-meal distribution.
goalModes.evidenceNote: Good trial evidence. Meta-analyses of resistance-training studies find added benefit up to roughly 1.6 g/kg/day, with diminishing returns above that; 2.2 g/kg is the upper bound of what trials have tested, not a requirement.

goalModes.name: Low bloat
goalModes.description: Flags high-FODMAP foods, sugar alcohols, carbonation, and high sodium; tracks how fast fiber intake is ramping.
goalModes.evidenceNote: FODMAP restriction has good randomised-trial evidence for bloating in IBS, with roughly 70% of participants improving. It is designed as a short elimination followed by structured reintroduction, not a permanent diet — long-term restriction reduces beneficial gut bacteria.

goalModes.name: Lower glycemic / skin
goalModes.description: Surfaces glycemic load per meal, flags high-GL meals, and emphasises zinc and omega-3.
goalModes.evidenceNote: The link between low-glycemic-load diets and acne rests on a small number of randomised trials plus consistent observational data — associated, not established. The dairy association is observational only, and the dairy flag is off by default for that reason.
